newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 266,000T corns/soybeans-trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 266,000T corns/soybeans-trade.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 128,000 tonnes of corn and 138,000 tonnes of soybeans this week if prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) dip, traders said on Monday.
"Buyers are all waiting to finish their September and October supplies," a grains trader said. "If Chicago futures have major drops in the next few days, they will all jump in."
Taiwanese buyers noted that rain had fallen across parts of the U.S. Midwest corn and soybean growing areas and said this may be a bearish factor when the CBOT opens later in the day.
"Rain over the weekend and additional rain forecast for Monday in parts of U.S. corn and soybean belts can keep the futures market in a bearish mood for now," a buyer said.
Taiwan still needed 128,000 tonnes of corn and 138,000 tonnes of soybeans to finish their requirements for September and October, traders said.
Taiwan's CK Group, Hui Shung Group and Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association were all expected to place tenders if Chicago futures prices ease, they added.
Egypt's decision to ban genetically modified grain or soybeans coming from the U.S. had no visible impact in Taiwan.
"Taiwan government does not require importers or suppliers to provide clear labelling of any gene-modified products, so we would not know anyway," a buyer said.
Traders said some U.S. trading companies had tried to promote U.S. gene-modified soybeans, which has a higher oil production yield rate, but buyers were put off by higher prices.
"Those gene-modified soybeans were too expensive, so no one bought them," a buyer said.
Wheat buyers, however, were expected to stay on the sidelines since Taiwan's near-term needs have already been filled, dealers said.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about US$11.50 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $21.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized September shipments.
